newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Swiss hunger, weak rand take Richemont high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss hunger, weak rand take Richemont high.

text.p: Hungry buying out of Switzerland and demand for rand hedge stocks pushed Richemont Securities to its highest level in seven months on Wednesday but dealers said the share could soon slow its climb.

The local listing of Swiss-based Compagnie Financiere Richemont AG, which announced higher year sales revenue last week, jumped to 71 rand from its Tuesday close of 69 rand before retreating slightly to 70.75 rand by 1045 GMT.
The tobacco and luxury products group last touched 71 rand on November 29, 1996.
Nearly a million shares worth over 65 million rand changed hands by 1045 GMT as the stock was snapped up.
"Richemont is a big rand hedge stock but also its results in Swiss franks were pretty good. There is quite a bit of buying out of Switzerland," said Paul Nettleton of Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.

Richemont last Thursday posted a 4.2 percent drop in attributable profit to 302.9 million sterling for the year ended March 31. But dealers said the number translated into more than satisfactory earnings in Swiss franks.
Furthermore, Richemont's net sales revenue was up 10.4 percent at 4.756 billion sterling and it increased its dividend per unit to 9.40 sterling from 8.00 sterling previously.
But the share drew most of its interest from offering an opportunity to hedge against weakness in the rand.

Although steady against the dollar on Wednesday -- last bid at 4.5310 -- the rand's decline since last week had reminded investors of its forecast further weakness in the second half of this year, dealers said.
A recent Reuters poll of 31 economists predicted that the rand would weaken to 4.68 against the U.S. dollar by the end of the year and further to 4.97 by the end of 1998.
Companies earning most of their income offshore become attractive when the South African currency weakens.
But dealers said the South African listed share was likely to level off soon and perhaps dip as profit was taken.
"They've had a good run and so I'm not sure that they'll go much higher," Nettleton said
Richemont's tobacco interests are held through Rothmans International, whose brands include Rothmans, Dunhill, Peter Stuyvesant and Craven "A".
Its luxury goods brands besides Dunhill include Cartier, Montblanc, Piaget, Baume & Mercier and Vacheron Constantin.
